oGit 2.1.0 makes runners easy to scale: one token can register many of them, and a runner can take a single job and go away.

**Documentation:** https://svnix-solutions.github.io/ogit/. **Upgrading:** this release has a migration, so run `ogit migration` before starting the new server (the Docker image does this on start). Existing runners and one-time registration tokens keep working.

## New

- **Reusable registration tokens.** A registration token can now register any number of runners, for fleets and autoscalers. Give it a name and, optionally, an expiry date. One-time tokens, valid for an hour, are still the default. Revoking a reusable token stops new registrations; the runners it registered keep working. Manage them in the runner settings of a repository, a group or the site, or through the API.
- **Ephemeral runners.** `ogit runner register --ephemeral` registers a runner for one run, enforced by the server: it hands the runner a single run, deletes it when that run ends, and the runner process exits. If the run is requeued, the runner can take another one.
- **Offline runners are cleaned up.** Ephemeral runners and runners registered with a reusable token are removed after a day unseen, never during a run. Runners registered with a one-time token are kept and shown as offline.
- **The Compose showcase scales.** `docker compose up -d --scale runner=3` starts three runners from one reusable token, each registering itself on start.

## Fixes

- **Several runners on one Docker host.** Jobs of the same name could collide on their container names, and one runner's cleanup could remove another's containers. Each run's containers now have unique names.
- **A deleted runner stops.** `ogit runner run` now exits when the server no longer knows it, rather than retrying forever.

## Documentation

- The runner guide has a new section on running many runners.
- The Try it guide and the Actions reference cover reusable tokens and ephemeral runners.
